properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 16 at 2:59PM EDT until October 16 at 3:30PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
SVRRLX

The National Weather Service in Charleston West Virginia has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Randolph County in northeastern West Virginia...
East central Lewis County in northern West Virginia...
Central Upshur County in northeastern West Virginia...
Southwestern Barbour County in northeastern West Virginia...

* Until 330 PM EDT.

* At 258 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Buckhannon,
moving east at 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Buckhannon, Audra State Park, Belington, Junior, Womelsdorf
(Coalton), Ellamore, Lorentz, Tallmansville, Overhill, Horner, and
French Creek.

This includes Route 33 between mile markers 2 and 31.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 1:59PM CDT until October 18 at 10:32AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP, Texas
affecting Brewster County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village,
BBNP,  Texas...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande at Rio Grande Village, BBNP,
Texas.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, and no damage
is expected.  Preparations may be necessary to remove water pumps.
The park should be notified at this time if additional rises are
expected so they will have time to remove the pumps. At 13.0 feet,
the river reaches minor flood stage.  Water reaches the water pumps
maintained by the park service that are used to water the
campgrounds and to provide water to the employee living quarters.
It may be necessary for park personnel to remove the pumps. At 15.0
feet, the river reaches moderate flood stage.  Water pumps
submerge.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:00 PM CDT Friday the stage was 1.3 feet (0.4 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet (3.7 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 16.4 feet (5.0 meters) late this
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late this evening.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet (4.0 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.4
feet (5.0 meters) on 08/12/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM CDT.

properties.description:
At 256 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
over Muncy to over Mifflinburg, moving east at 50 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to trees, roofs, and siding.

Locations impacted include...
Williamsport, Milton, Lewisburg, Montoursville, Northumberland,
Mifflinburg, Winfield, Muncy, Watsontown, Hughesville, Montgomery,
Linntown, Duboistown, New Columbia, Montandon, Allenwood,
Vicksburg, Delaware Run, Spruce Run Reservoir and Elimsport.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 180 between mile markers 1 and 29. Interstate 80 between
mile markers 195 and 219. Interstate 99 between mile markers 136 and
139.
properties.instruction:

windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

properties.areaDesc: Hatteras Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 16 at 2:55PM EDT until October 20 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to
12 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Watch,
2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM Saturday to 8 AM
EDT Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Saturday
afternoon through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of vehicles
will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be inundated,
especially around high tide. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash impacts
to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high tide cycles
into next week. Minor soundside water level rises will also be
possible.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.
